issues.body: Step C still says to run `python3 scripts/ledger-invariant.py` against a fresh checkout of the rewritten branch. The shipped CLI requires a positional `root`, so the literal command exits in argparse without checking the tree. Moreover, the rewritten `ledger` checkout is intentionally data-only and therefore has no `scripts/ledger-invariant.py` to execute. The later contents-API and parser checks validate tip content, but they do not make this separately prescribed allowlist/tree-shape check executable. This is the same major defect recorded in round 3.
issues.fix_hint: Name two distinct checkouts and an exact executable command: invoke `scripts/ledger-invariant.py` from a trusted registry code checkout at a specified reviewed SHA, and pass the fresh rewritten-ledger checkout as the positional root, for example `python3 <registry-code-checkout>/scripts/ledger-invariant.py <rewritten-ledger-checkout>`. Keep the code source and validation target explicit and distinct.
issues.title: The ledger-invariant post-check still cannot run as written

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-3 major finding remains materially unchanged. Step C still prescribes `python3 scripts/ledger-invariant.py` against a fresh rewritten-ledger checkout, but that program requires the checkout root as a positional argument and the data-only ledger checkout does not contain `scripts/ledger-invariant.py`. The surrounding new API checks do not repair this first, explicitly required tree-shape gate. The runbook therefore still is not executable as written before writers resume.
